title: Ask run-parts what it would actually run, not what's sitting in the directory
explanation: The file `/etc/cron.daily/backup` existing on disk doesn't mean cron's daily runner will touch it. `run-parts --test /etc/cron.daily` prints exactly what the real invocation would execute — and `backup` is conspicuously absent from that list even though `ls /etc/cron.daily/` shows it's there. That gap is the whole bug, before you've even opened the script.

title: run-parts has its own silent admission criteria
explanation: `run-parts` (what cron actually uses to execute everything under `/etc/cron.daily|weekly|monthly`) skips any file that isn't executable, and separately skips filenames containing a `.` (so `backup.sh` would be ignored too, for a different reason). Neither exclusion produces an error, a log line, or any output anywhere — a skipped script looks identical to a script that ran and did nothing.

title: Confirm the specific gap before changing anything
explanation: `ls -l /etc/cron.daily/backup` shows `-rw-r--r--` (644) — no `x` bit for anyone, including the owner. That's the concrete reason `run-parts --test` left it out, and it also explains the misleading "but it works when I run it by hand" observation: `sh backup` invokes the interpreter directly and never needs the file's own execute permission, so manual testing doesn't reproduce the bug at all.

title: Grant exactly the bit run-parts checks for
explanation: `sudo chmod +x /etc/cron.daily/backup` adds the execute bit without touching anything else about the file's permissions or content — the script itself was never broken, only its eligibility to be picked up.

title: Verify with the same tool that revealed the problem, then for real
explanation: `run-parts --test /etc/cron.daily` now lists `backup`, confirming it's eligible again. Running it for real (`sudo run-parts /etc/cron.daily`) and finding `/var/backups/app-backup.tar` on disk confirms the whole chain — eligibility *and* execution — actually works, not just the permission bit in isolation.
